newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - APIs seen supporting NYMEX, spot heat oil.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - APIs seen supporting NYMEX, spot heat oil.

text.p: Tuesday evening's inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) provided few surprises, but traders and analysts agreed heating oil got the best of the report's bullishness.
NYMEX traders agreed, bidding December heat up 0.50 cent in after-hours ACCESS trade to 71.85/72.00 cents a gallon.

"The numbers are bullish for New York heat," one trader said of the report, which showed East Coast heating oil stocks falling by just over a million barrels last week to 30.2 million barrels. The overall distillate number was a deceptively bearish rise of 660,000 barrels to 118.2 million.

Still, distillate output, at 3.61 million barrels a day (bpd), remained near record levels, which could mute traders' bullish response to the East Coast stock drop since most demand is met by current production and not stocks.
That easily outpaces the previous November record of 3.47 million bpd set in 1993, said API statistician Ron Planting.
But traders point to the rise in Gulf Coast heating oil and low sulphur diesel stocks as one reason the New York Harbor (NYH) market ought to stay firm.
"There's a chokehold which prevents a lot of it from reaching NYH where it's really needed," a trader said.

He said much of the Gulf material has no economical way of reaching New York because the Colonial Pipeline has extended space allocation on its 960,000 barrel per day Houston-to-New York distillate line through the month of December.
A Dean Witter analyst agreed the numbers were "supportive" for New York heat, but said the overall distillate data were neutral to somewhat bearish.

"We were looking for a decline on distillate stocks and it came in as a build contrary to what you'd expect during the heating season," he said, though he acknowledged that the East Coast heating oil stock drop was somewhat bullish.

Gasoline futures were meanwhile little changed, after API said total U.S. stocks fell 637,000 barrels for the week ending November 22, though stronger imports helped lift stocks of East Coast reformulated-grade fuel by 770,000 barrels.
"The numbers are bullish for gasoline because supplies are tight everywhere on most grades," one Houston trader said.

U.S. refineries were operating at 93.7 percent of capacity, compared with 92.9 percent the prior week, a factor that helped draw down crude stocks by 2.03 million barrels to 300.3 million, API said. January crude on ACCESS advanced about 10 cents to $23.62 a barrel.
